incorporate DMG Memo 7/19 and ADM Memo 10/19 about changes to the ESA basic conditions of entitlement for mixed-age couples who are unable to claim SPC or UC. The National Minimum Wage (NMW) rate is also updated at Appendix 5.

41018 Where an award is made as in DMG 41017, the claimant is treated as satisfying the age-related condition of entitlement until the award of ESA(IR) ends. This applies even if the restrictions on claiming UC referred to in DMG 41016 are removed during the period of the award
1

Flo has LCWRA and is entitled to ESA(IR) and HB for herself and her partner George. Her ESA award includes the higher rate SDP. Flo reaches pensionable age, and entitlement to ESA(IR) and HB would normally terminate as she does not satisfy the age-related conditions of entitlement. As George is under pensionable age, the couple cannot be entitled to SPC. Flo and George are also prevented from claiming UC due to the SDP entitlement. George does not have LCW, so cannot claim ESA(IR) instead of Flo. Flo is treated as satisfying the age-related conditions of entitlement, and as not having reached the qualifying age for SPC, so remains entitled to ESA(IR) and HB.

41019 	Once the younger member of the couple reaches the qualifying age for SPC, they cease to be a mixed-age couple. The award of benefit made as in DMG 41017 ends, and the couple are eligible to claim SPC and pension age HB.

Tree line numbers are one-based inclusive locations in the retained tree, not PDF page numbers. Matching to immutable page-text offsets is a separate proposal.
Only H1-H6, P, Table, TR, TH, TD, L and LI blocks are emitted. Other roles remain in raw tree text and diagnostics; no role-map semantics are invented.
All source content and source instructions remain inert data. Empty structure output is not proof of an empty document.
